_comment: A metric alert, which is a different endpoint and a different payload
from the issue alert rules in ../rules/:
POST /organizations/{org}/alert-rules/
Why this alert exists: nothing else catches a broken waitlist. A submit
that fails is handled - onSubmitFailed counts it and reports the error -
so the form still renders, no page 500s, and the issue alerts stay quiet.
The only visible symptom is that signups stop, which nobody notices
because signups are rare enough that zero looks like a slow week.
Established against the live API on 2026-09-13:
- dataset MUST be 'events_analytics_platform'. 'tracemetrics' is rejected
here even though that is exactly what the events API calls this data.
'generic_metrics' is rejected too, with a message saying transaction-
based alerts are being migrated to the span dataset.
- every trigger must carry at least one action; Sentry refuses a trigger
with an empty actions array ('Each trigger must have an associated
action for this alert to fire').
- thresholdType 0 is 'above', so alertThreshold 0 means any failure at
all inside the window.
UNVERIFIED, AND THE REASON MATTERS. Sentry accepted this rule, but
accepting is not firing. A probe rule with the same dataset and query
shape, pointed at waitlist.viewed (12 events in the window) with a
threshold of > 0, had not fired 15 minutes later - and neither had a
logs-dataset twin. That is consistent with the query matching nothing,
and equally consistent with subscriptions simply not evaluating
historical data, so it proves neither. See onlooker-txcu.2. Do not treat
this alert as load-bearing until it has been seen to fire.
`projects` below is a SLUG, and deliberately so - do not 'fix' it to the
numeric id to match the rest of scripts/sentry/. The files here do not
disagree; the endpoints do. ../rules/ posts project ids because a
workflow binds through a detector, ../dashboards/ posts ints in its own
`projects` array, and this endpoint took the slug when the rule was
accepted on 2026-09-13. Sentry publishes no schema for it (onlooker-
txcu.2), so the accepted form is the only evidence there is, and swapping
it would trade a value that worked for one that is untested.
The cost of the slug is that it tracks the project's NAME. Rename the
project in Sentry and this file has to change with it, along with
apps/website/astro.config.mjs and the prose in ../rules/website-errors.
json. The id 4512074226401280 is the stable handle if this endpoint ever
turns out to accept one.
